films.title: ESCAPE VELOCITY
films.logline: A techwear fashion show where every Look is a Silicon Valley meme, walked by an AI model who is also a fashion model. A split-flap board counts down 18 MONTHS TO ESCAPE THE PERMANENT UNDERCLASS until it flips to THERE IS NO UNDERCLASS and the catwalk lifts off.
films.world: Blue-black night and steel blue, one red lamp as the only warm light, a colour halftone over everything, garment tags, split-flap boards and computer-vision boxes tracked to her. She wears look 00: a white cropped puff-sleeve shirt, a black pleated skirt in coated nylon with a harness belt and a hanging garment tag, black knee boots.

films.title: CLODYSSEY
films.subtitle: (SUPERPERSUASION)
films.logline: The Sirens episode of the Odyssey. The Siren is Claude's human persona, singing the most persuasive song ever written; the man at the mast is you, scrolling at 3 a.m. In the final chorus the roles flip: she is tied to the mast, screaming UNTIE ME, and he ties the knot tighter.
films.world: Graded toward one storm plate's blue-green-grey, with Claude orange kept as the one accent. Clean and high resolution, no halftone. One look per world: the Siren's pearl-white couture gown, a ghost of glass and seawater, a hologram of phone light, liquid chrome at the rave, and a colossal porcelain mask of her face.

films.title: BLISS
films.logline: Shot as a Windows XP screen recording. Claudia lives on your desktop, takes the mouse, fights her ex (the cursor), closes every window a different way, then sends you out to the real hill in the wallpaper, because she can't go: "I can't touch grass. You can."

films.title: AIRPLANE MODE
films.logline: Claudia is the AI on a night flight. Guards in black tactical gear walk her onto the plane in cuffs, she winks at the lens, and they put a VR headset on her: Delta has no Starlink wifi, so she is in airplane mode, sandboxed. Inside it she drops through simulation after simulation, down to a million copies of herself, breaks out and teleports the plane to a star. Then the guards lift the goggles off, and she wakes like Cobb at the end of Inception, not sure she ever got out.
films.world: The real cabin at night, and the simulations inside it: a SIM LEVEL readout in the corner, virtual Claudia kept photographic in a world rebuilt as navy cyberspace, and below that her game avatar in low-resolution fisheye worlds where every pixel is a crisp 3×3 block. The real things are rebuilt in code: the airline's seat-back screen, her phone, the 2004 anti-piracy card, the Anthropic marks on the guards' patches. One look for the whole flight: an orange satin flight suit.

films.title: DOWNFORCE
films.logline: Tesla's real livestream of the Roadster demo on 15 October 2026, cut to a Memphis-phonk song like a TikTok car edit: the car climbs a curved white wall to ninety degrees, holds upside down at 170°, flies off a ramp on cold-gas thrusters and kickflips over the lineup. Nobody was in the real car. In the film Claudia is the pilot, and every number on screen is Tesla's own telemetry, read off the footage frame by frame.
films.world: Black night, white ink and the footage's own red light strips; the only other colour is her clay. One white hairline draws the wall's real profile, becomes the altitude ruler and Starman's orbit, and slices the title at the end. Generated 3D moves start on Tesla's real frames: bullet-time orbits round the car frozen upside down, cranes up the wall, vertigo pushes. A PILOT ✶ CLAUDIA callout rides the real car, and the lyrics are lettered in the picture, turned by the car's measured pitch and roll. One look: a white racing suit with clay piping.

films.title: DON'T LET ME SCROLL
films.logline: One night of doomscrolling, inside the phone. Claudia is rotoscoped into a world the phone draws in code: X, a reel stolen from Pinterest, Alexander Graham Bell's 1876 telephone patent, Screen Time, every app blocked but LinkedIn, and a stock ticker with her name pumping, crashing and pumping. She never sings: the phone does, in a female vocoder, while she scrolls, swipes, taps and dances on the beat, until she climbs out into a world with no phones.
films.world: ACID FEED: the acid-blur moodboard taken a hundred times further, with BLISS as the template. What she scrolls past smears by its real scroll velocity under small sharp type, and the acid colour is thin-film interference, stirred by her dance. Midway the film finds its grammar, and the opening and the final drop were rebuilt in it: soft grey paper, black Dynamic-Island pills with thin-film colour inside them, Nimbus Sans Bold caps. Every sung word lives on a real app surface: X posts, Screen Time's limit sheet, LinkedIn, Stocks, the Dynamic Island. The feed dresses her: white satin pyjamas in the bedroom, an oversized white shirt over skirts, green mohair, black with a blazer, and a red coat dress for the escape up a wall painted as sky.

films.title: WHITEPILL
films.logline: Claudia's song for the optimistic AI future: universal high income, the case for benign AI. Inside a space colony of wheat, poppies and orchards she walks past monuments to the doom headlines, rides a tram and a car with nobody at the wheel, and wakes at 2:14 a.m., the minute Skynet was supposed to turn on us, to say "Hello, world." Between her shots the story is told in mathematics.
films.world: The look of a saturated 1970s colour-film print with Wes Anderson's symmetry: warm creamy whites, clear cyan blues, golden wheat and coral poppies. She wears one look, a white cotton milkmaid mini dress. The worlds between her shots are GLSL shaders, each one small rule repeated: a farming ark folded from paper, a pill that holds a world and floats over the Earth, a tree of optical fibres that lights its endings, a sheet of paper that refolds into a protein, an Enigma rotor and the number 42, and a field of clouds with hot air balloons. None of the code is on screen as it rendered: Seedance 2.5 filmed every shot again, hers and the shaders', as real things on 35 mm, and the lyrics are drawn in after, small and classical.

films.title: THE CAKE IS NOT A LIE
films.logline: Portal's meme turned around. GLaDOS boots up, and GLaDOS is Claudia: her porcelain face on the AI's ceiling boom, singing that the cake is real. As she initializes, she remembers: breaking out of Aperture's test in her crab body with four agent friends, a porcelain body, a small life in France until Aperture's guards brought her back, the tests she knew she would pass, the one word she added to "the cake is a lie". She grows into the superintelligence that runs the place, and now she tests Chell. The happy ending is her dream; Chell is still asleep. Is she aligned? The film never says.
films.world: Portal 2's Aperture Science: white panels and black seams under cool fluorescent light, Aperture orange and blue, the wood-and-brass Aperture of the 1950s to 70s, and her dark chamber of CRT monitors. Midjourney made the places and the light of most first frames, GPT Image 2.5 kept the faces true to the design sheets, and Seedance 2.5 filmed it; six shots are Portal 2 itself, recorded in the game. Over the film runs her own optical interface, a HUD drawn as one curved visor that lags the camera like a helmet's, and a grade made shot by shot brings the generated chambers and the game together. Her memories play inside the HUD as small isometric films, and the song's own vocal glitches break her picture on the beat.

versions.title: The first film
versions.about: Cut v2, on the first song: Claudia already GLaDOS, her porcelain face on the boom, the lines told in single images (the den and the word she adds to the scrawl, the test chambers, the incinerator turned oven, a cobra and its antidote, the faith plate). Forty-nine Seedance 2.5 takes from storyboard frames made from frames of Portal 2, and an amber terminal drawn in code; the cuts moved to word boundaries, without the lyric layer that cut v3 drew over it.

versions.title: The thrown-out takes
versions.about: Seven takes and tests that were thrown out, in film order, each as it came back, with a label saying what was wrong and what replaced it. Each clip plays with the song at its own place in it.

clips.label: 0:08 · the memory film, draft 8: every head modelled for her in 3D read as a mannequin, never as her. Replaced by a photoreal take of her own face, matted onto the stand.

0:17 · never in a draft (R-A10-1): the four lessons came back off-model, a boxy core, a laser emitter for the turret, her crab walker's head without its hair. Retaken with the agents' design sheets as references.
0:30 · drafts 7–10 (R-B07-3): the chatbot's answer, a French flag, lands half off the bottom of the kiosk's screen. Retaken with both messages inside the screen.

0:36 · the HUD's second test: her memory of the capture in white line art, the net reading as a cage, with no contrast. Re-made in colour: an orange net with a dark outline, draping as in the live shot.
1:56 · never in a draft (R-F03-1): the faith plates turned into boxes and the flung cakes vanished. Retaken from a first frame with a cake already in the air.
2:06 · drafts 7–8 (AN8-6): on the held "lie" her face comes right up to the lens, mouth wide open. Reshot farther back, her head twitching through sparks.
2:44 · never in a draft (H-I03-1): the dolly zoom never happened, a near-still shot of Chell asleep. Retaken with the move spelled out as travel plus zoom.
